title: Deceased-determination policy v1 + living-person takedown workflow
context: Genealogy data is uniquely privacy-sensitive: dates of birth, birthplaces, and mothers' maiden names are common identity-verification secrets, and recent records routinely name living relatives. This project covers deceased persons only and requires a formal, versioned deceased-determination policy defining exactly when a person is treated as deceased (positive death evidence or documented birth ≥100 years prior) and what happens when a person cannot be classified. The policy must also specify which fields are categorically excluded (SSN, Death Master File/SSDI, genetic/DNA data) and define a takedown workflow for any living person inadvertently included.
objective: Author and version the deceased-determination policy v1, specifying the exact rule thresholds (the 100-year cutoff and definition of 'positive death evidence'), an explicit decision table for edge cases, exclusion of SSN/DMF/genetic fields, suppression of living relatives named in records, and a documented living-person takedown workflow with a ≤72h median SLA.
acceptanceCriteria: Deceased-determination rule v1 stated and versioned: a person is treated as deceased if (a) positive death evidence exists in a PD source, or (b) documented birth ≥100 years before the present; uncertainty defaults to exclusion.

Decision table covering all edge cases: positive death evidence, birth ≥100 years, birth <100 years without death evidence, age-only record implying living status, no birth/death evidence, mixed records with possibly-living relatives.
SSN, Death Master File / SSDI data, and genetic/DNA data exclusion stated as schema-level constraints, not policy-only.
Living-relative suppression rule stated: individuals enumerated who may be living (e.g., a child on a 1950 census) are suppressed, not published.
Takedown workflow documented: report → verify → remove (≤72h median SLA); removals logged without re-publishing PII; affected source batch re-audited after any confirmed living-person inclusion.
P0 incident protocol defined: confirmed living-person publication triggers immediate export pull, root-cause analysis, batch re-audit, and public post-mortem before re-release.
Policy published as a versioned document (docs/privacy-policy-v1.md) committed via PR.
output: docs/privacy-policy-v1.md — versioned deceased-determination policy, edge-case decision table, excluded-fields list, living-relative suppression rule, takedown workflow, and P0 incident protocol, committed via PR.
